about: The PySpark target half of the silent-differences catalogue (ADR 0019): where Spark's built-ins differ from the meaning the source gives the construct, and which built-in or treatment reproduces it. Its entries are Annex D's, keyed by the same IDs as the source half, and the engine's tests check every cell against docs/spec/annex-d-differences-pyspark.md. 'behaviour' is Spark's behaviour (with ANSI on, in section 1, where 'behaviour_ansi_off' is the other column). Only a target-only entry (9.14) holds its own example; the others' examples are the source half's. 'naive_built_in' is, where one exists, the built-in named in the entry's Spark cell that a direct conversion would emit and that the reproducing helper replaces, for mutation testing; the tests check the cell names it. 'wording' is the report's plain wording of Spark's behaviour, never of the source's. The version is the hash of 'entries'.

entries.section: 3. Numbers: division, implicit conversion, decimal precision
entries.behaviour: `sum` over an integral column accumulates in `BIGINT` ([Databricks `sum`][d-sum]), so no running total leaves `int`; cast to `INT`, the result fails under ANSI only when the final total does not fit
entries.reproduces: None. A helper that fails when a running total leaves `int` reproduces SQL Server for a given order of rows; since SQL Server's order is not defined, a caveat stays in the report wherever the helper is used
entries.evidence: SQL Server half tested on the 2022 CU27 sandbox for the order shown; the dependence on plan order and the Spark half are inferred. Added by the owner in [Engine skeleton: one view converted end to end as a preview run](https://github.com/Bach-To-The-Future/data-migration/issues/36)
entries.wording: Spark raises only when the final total does not fit

entries.behaviour: The timestamp keeps `.999`: six fractional digits are stored and nothing is rounded to a coarser grid ([Databricks TIMESTAMP][d-timestamp])
entries.reproduces: None. Matters for end-of-day predicates and for comparing against stored `datetime` values

entries.behaviour: The timestamp keeps the seconds ([Databricks TIMESTAMP][d-timestamp])
entries.reproduces: None. Emulate by adding 30 seconds and truncating to the minute

entries.behaviour: Six fractional digits by default; extra digits in a string or cast are truncated. Databricks `TIMESTAMP(p)` with 7 to 9 digits is in Beta ([Databricks TIMESTAMP][d-timestamp], [Databricks `cast`][d-cast])
entries.reproduces: None outside the Beta type

entries.behaviour: `TIMESTAMP` is an absolute instant shown in the session time zone; the offset is not kept ([Spark data types][s-types])
entries.reproduces: None. Carry the offset in a separate column

entries.behaviour: `TIMESTAMP` is interpreted in the session time zone, so the same stored value reads differently when the session zone changes; `TIMESTAMP_NTZ` ignores time zones ([Spark data types][s-types])
entries.reproduces: `TIMESTAMP_NTZ`

entries.behaviour: `current_timestamp()` in the session time zone, which defaults to UTC in Databricks SQL and to the JVM's zone in Apache Spark ([Databricks TIMEZONE][d-timezone], [Spark configuration][s-config])
entries.reproduces: Set the session time zone to the source server's zone

entries.behaviour: `0` (derived): `datediff(unit, start, end)` and `timestamp_diff` count whole elapsed units ([Databricks `datediff` (timestamp)][d-datediff3], [PySpark `timestamp_diff`][p-tsdiff])
entries.reproduces: None single. Year: `year(end) - year(start)`. Month: year difference times 12 plus month difference. Day: two-argument `datediff` on dates. Smaller units: truncate both sides with `date_trunc`, then difference

Databricks has `GET DIAGNOSTICS … ROW_COUNT` for the latest DML statement, only inside a SQL compound statement (Runtime 18 LTS+) ([GET DIAGNOSTICS][d-getdiag]). entries.behaviour: By default each statement is its own transaction against one table, and nothing spans statements, so a generated "rollback" leaves the earlier writes committed ([Databricks ACID][d-acid])

Apache Spark with Delta: none ([Delta concurrency][dl-cc])

entries.behaviour: An uncaught Python exception stops the script at the second statement, so the third never runs. This is Python's behaviour and is not stated in the Spark documentation

entries.reproduces: None found
